primary_claim: Concept Activation Vector (CAV) steering, using an automatic all-layer perturbation algorithm, reliably steers Llama-3-8B-Instruct's output style toward existing capabilities (e.g. French-language responses, Python-code responses) with high classifier accuracy (98-99%), but cannot elicit capabilities the model does not already have (e.g. fluent Arabic or base64 output) -- it can only transfer between existing capabilities.

effect.metric: CAV linear classifier test accuracy / qualitative steering success
effect.value: Python-expert classifier accuracy 99%; French-format-1 classifier accuracy >98% (all layers except layer 0)

contradicts_or_qualifies: qualifies comparison to Anthropic's SAE-based feature steering: attempting to reproduce Anthropic's reported Arabic/base64 feature steering via CAVs was much less effective, likely due to the model's own capability limits rather than the steering method
stated_future_work: Quick alignment of agent functions -- replacing system prompts with CAV steering
Effects of multiple CAVs steering simultaneously
As a probe for LLM capabilities, e.g. to detect whether specific abilities are still present after unlearning
Mathematical association with SAE features -- combining SAE features and CAVs
limitations_stated: CAV steering cannot create the capabilities that the model does not have out of thin air, but can only transfer between existing capabilities
the quality of the generated text was slightly affected [when steering], with some repetitions
This highlights the instability of the technique [sensitivity to the P0 threshold]
the steering results were not as effective [for Arabic/base64 features], often being cut off or nonsensical
quote: CAV steering cannot create the capabilities that the model does not have out of thin air, but can only transfer between existing capabilities, which is a bit like system prompts.
